audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says Neeko 'pops it from under a W clone disguise' and tells the player to 'check the clone first'. The disguise and the clone are two different abilities, and only one of them hides Pop Blossom.
audit.why: Riot's text: Inherent Glamour (P) is the disguise — 'Neeko can look like an ally champion or as other units on the map.' Shapesplitter (W) is a clone she sends off in a direction and can redirect; it is not a disguise she wears. Pop Blossom's text is specific: 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised.' So the thing that hides the wind-up is the passive, not the W. A player watching for the clone is watching the wrong tell.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text, mid and wants.foe[2] now say Inherent Glamour, and Shapesplitter is described for what it actually is.
sources: champ-data/_kits/neeko.json (P Inherent Glamour, W Shapesplitter, R Pop Blossom)

audit.whatIsWrong: Inherent Glamour's break conditions are never stated, and one of them is the single best thing Ambessa's kit does in this matchup.
audit.why: Riot's text: the disguise breaks on 'receiving immobilizing crowd control, casting damaging spells, damaging enemy towers as a non-champion, or your disguise taking damage equal to its healthbar.' Public Execution suppresses on arrival and then stuns — both immobilizing — so it strips a disguised Neeko outright. It also means she cannot open a fight from disguise: the first damaging spell she casts reveals her regardless.
audit.corrected: Added to spikes[2].text, mid and whys[4].

audit.whatIsWrong: Tangle-Barbs is described only as a root, in an entry where dodging it is the whole early game.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Neeko slings a tangle that damages and roots everything it passes through. If the tangle kills an enemy or passes through a champion, it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer.' Two consequences the entry misses: it does not stop on minions, so standing behind the wave does not block it — and a low minion it kills on the way makes the root that reaches you bigger, faster and longer. It is 12s at rank 1 from 1000 range.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, early, whys[2] and wants.foe[0] now carry the upgrade rule and the 12s.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Your R's flat armor pen' and 'burst her squishy frame with armor-pen damage' appear in spikes[1].text, wants.you[1], mid and whys[4], and no real cooldown appears anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Public Execution has no penetration and no passive — Riot's text is a 1250-range blink to the farthest enemy champion in a line, a suppression on arrival, then a slam that damages and stuns. The numbers that do matter and were absent: Blooming Burst 9s at rank 1 from 800, Tangle-Barbs 12s from 1000, Shapesplitter 16s, Pop Blossom 120s against Public Execution's 130s.
audit.corrected: Penetration removed from all four; the suppression and the disguise-break replace it, and the cooldowns are now in spikes[0].text, early, mid, whys[1], whys[3] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pop Blossom is called 'an unstoppable AOE stun' twice.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'After a short preparation, Neeko leaps into the air, knocking up all nearby enemies. Upon landing, nearby enemies are damaged and stunned.' Nothing in it says unstoppable, and Neeko's kit file carries no unstoppable flag. The real property worth knowing is the short preparation — visible unless she is disguised — and the 600 range, which is short enough to walk out of.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text and mid now describe the preparation and the 600 range instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shapesplitter's passive is never mentioned, so her poke damage is credited entirely to Blooming Burst.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Neeko passively deals bonus magic damage every third attack, briefly increasing her move speed.' It is a three-auto counter that also gives her the speed to walk away from a step-up — part of why the level 1-2 exchanges go her way and why she is hard to close on.

edits.before: Neeko owns this opening more than most melees you face. Her Q (Blooming Burst) bounces for poke and her E (Tangle-Barbs) roots from a range your kit can't answer before your abilities are up, so don't walk up to free-cast — your Q is your only gap-closer at level 1 and you're energy-gated early. The trade pattern: last-hit at max range, accept a little Q poke, and never commit a Drakehound's Step dash into an obvious E-root angle — if she lands the root you're stuck eating her full rotation. Bait the E, then look for a short Q-cone-into-Sundering-Slam tap when it's down, but don't extend.
edits.after: Neeko owns this opening more than most melees you face. Blooming Burst pokes from 800 every 9s and Tangle-Barbs roots from 1000 through everything in its path, so hiding behind the wave does nothing — worse, a minion the tangle kills on the way makes the root that finally reaches you bigger, faster and longer. Last-hit at max range, accept a little Q poke, and never commit a Drakehound's Step dash into an obvious root angle: if she lands it you eat her whole rotation. Bait the E, then take a short Q-cone-into-Sundering-Slam tap on its 12s, and don't extend.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay rough — her root-into-poke combo out-trades your cooldowns, so keep farming toward 6 and don't force. Level 6 is the lane's pivot: Public Execution blinks you behind her, suppresses, and crashes down with armor-pen burst plus a brief stun, and Neeko is squishy enough that a clean R-into-Q-into-empowered-auto can outright kill her before she buys Zhonya's. The catch is her own 6 — Pop Blossom is an unstoppable AOE stun, and she'll often pop it from under her W clone disguise. Check the clone, bait her R or her Flash, then commit; an R thrown into a hidden clone is a wasted ult and a free reset for her.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay rough — her root-into-poke combo out-trades your cooldowns, so keep farming toward 6 and don't force. Level 6 is the lane's pivot: Public Execution blinks 1250 to the farthest champion in the line, suppresses her and slams her down, and because the immobilize breaks Inherent Glamour a disguised Neeko is stripped the moment you land. Her own 6 is Pop Blossom: a short preparation inside a 600 radius, hidden only while she is disguised. Read the disguise rather than the clone, bait her R or her Flash, then commit — an R spent into a decoy is a free reset for her.

edits.before: Once Neeko has Zhonya's plus a second AP item this slips away. Her stopwatch eats your R suppress-burst exactly when you'd kill her, and a fed full-AP Neeko bursts you from outside your dash range — your physical-only damage can't drop her health bar fast enough. She also becomes a roam-and-pick threat with her clone disguise, so the map gets dangerous, not just the lane. Your only real path is to have already snowballed off your Level 6 and first-item windows; if it's even at 2 items, group with your team and don't get caught alone facechecking for her clone.

notes: The load-bearing confusion was between two different Neeko abilities. Inherent Glamour (P) is the disguise, and it is what hides Pop Blossom's wind-up; Shapesplitter (W) is a redirectable clone she sends away from herself. The entry told the player to 'check the clone' before committing, which watches the wrong thing. The passive also breaks on immobilizing crowd control, which makes Public Execution's suppression a disguise-stripper — the strongest true statement available for the level-6 row, and it replaced the invented 'flat armor pen' that was there instead. Tangle-Barbs passing through everything (and upgrading off a minion it kills) is the other correction that changes behaviour: standing behind the wave is not cover. I did not repeat 'unstoppable' for Pop Blossom — Riot's text does not say it and the kit carries no such flag.
